$comment: PRODUCT READINESS, and how every figure in it is derived (PW phase, round 80).
THIS IS NOT THE ENGINEERING COMPLETION FIGURE AND MUST NEVER BE COMPARED TO IT.
coordination/PROJECT_STATUS.md reports DONE/total over control/tasks.json; that
answers 'has the board been worked'. This file answers a different question --
'can a person install this on a Windows PC and watch something' -- and the two
were 62/64 and roughly one third of the way there on the same tree, which is
exactly why they are separate files.
DERIVATION, stated so it cannot quietly become a task count. Each dimension
lists CAPABILITIES a user would notice. Each capability is scored:
present = 1.0   implemented AND reachable by a user of the shipped app
partial = 0.5   implemented behind a seam a user cannot reach, or
implemented for one target/case but not the shipped one
absent  = 0.0   no implementation
A dimension's figure is the sum of its item scores over its item count.
Overall is the WEIGHTED mean of the dimensions, using the weights below --
not a mean of means, because the dimensions are not equally load-bearing for
'can a person watch something'.
WHY 'partial' EXISTS AND IS NOT A HEDGE. Three capabilities in this product --
profiles, watchlist, progress -- have complete, tested, reviewed HTTP APIs and
no user interface whatsoever. Scoring them absent would erase real reviewed
work; scoring them present would claim a person can use them. 0.5 is the only
honest answer and the evidence field says which half exists.
EVERY item's `evidence` is a repository path or an explicit statement of
absence. An item with no evidence is a defect in this file.
Weighted because the dimensions are not equally load-bearing for a usable
Windows product. nativePlayback and windowsDesktop are weighted highest
because without them there is no Windows application at all, whatever the
rest scores. engineeringFoundation is weighted LOW despite being nearly
complete, for the same reason: it is necessary and it is not sufficient,
and weighting it high would let a finished foundation flatter the figure.
